description: Rich visual character descriptions for all 19 Gray-Scott / Pearson pattern types. Designed for use in generative AI workflows, prompt engineering, and creative tool integration.

types.name: Uniform Red
types.visual_character: A featureless, chemically exhausted plane. No structure emerges — the activator (V) is fully consumed and the field settles to a deep, flat red. Visually analogous to an overexposed photographic plate or an annealed metal surface.
types.emergence_behavior: Starting from any seed condition, transient waves quickly decay. Within a few hundred iterations the entire field collapses to the uniform low-V state. No stable structures survive.

color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: No contrast available. Best used as a reference or void space.

types.name: Uniform Blue
types.visual_character: The opposite extreme from R — a uniformly saturated, calm, featureless field in which U dominates completely. Imagine a still, deep-blue ocean surface with no wind, no ripples, no life.
types.emergence_behavior: Any perturbation rapidly smooths out. Feed rate is high enough to replenish U faster than V can consume it. All patterns dissolve into the calm equilibrium.

color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Pair with type R as a diptych — perfect contrast of extremes.

types.name: Wavelet Chaos
types.visual_character: A turbulent, never-settling sea of short-lived wave packets and nascent spirals. Reminiscent of disturbed water viewed from above — patches of coherent wavelets constantly forming, colliding, and dissolving. No two moments are the same.
types.emergence_behavior: Immediately active from any seed. Spirals emerge, rotate briefly, then destabilize as neighboring spirals collide. The system never reaches steady state — it sustains continuous spatiotemporal chaos indefinitely.
types.visual_scale: Medium wavelength. Coherent patches span roughly 15–40 pixels at 512² resolution.
types.density: Moderate. Roughly 30–40% of the field is in the V-rich (activated) state at any moment.

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: dark teal to bright cyan (V channel), or inferno colormap for activity
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Use du/dt coloring (Munafo mode) to highlight the most active wavefronts in vivid white.

types.name: Ocean Voids
types.visual_character: A sweeping blue field periodically interrupted by red voids — dark holes punched through a luminous ocean. The voids drift, merge, and spawn new ones in a slow, stately rhythm. Like viewing bioluminescent plankton blooms from altitude, with dark dead patches drifting through.
types.emergence_behavior: Begins with spiral-wave activity similar to α. Over hundreds of iterations, the spirals organize into larger-scale traveling waves. Periodic voids (low-V regions) appear, grow, and are swept by the wavefronts. Motion is sustained chaotically.
types.visual_scale: Large-scale voids (50–100 pixels diameter) embedded in fine wave texture.
types.density: Low to moderate V density. Voids occupy 20–40% of field.
ai_prompt_keywords: bioluminescent ocean waves with dark voids
dark holes drifting through luminous fluid
periodic void patterns in chemical waves

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: deep navy to electric blue (waves), black (voids)
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Invert the V channel for a white-on-dark display reminiscent of medical imaging.

types.name: Unstable Stripes
types.visual_character: Sinuous, worm-like stripes that constantly rearrange themselves. Grain boundaries form and dissolve — the stripes align locally but never globally. The texture looks like fingerprint ridges or wood grain that never settles, always rearranging its direction.
types.emergence_behavior: Stripes emerge within the first 500–1000 iterations from a disordered seed. Grain boundary events — T-junctions, stripe endings, curvature-driven reorientation — continue indefinitely. The system is periodic (oscillatory) in local character but never globally static.
types.visual_scale: Stripe wavelength ~10–20 pixels at 512². Multiple grain domains of 50–150 pixel extent.
types.density: Moderate. Stripes cover roughly 40–60% of the field.

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: warm cream to burnt sienna (wood grain feel), or black-to-white for fingerprint aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Threshold at V=0.2 for a binary stripe rendering. Animate the threshold to show wave motion.

types.name: Turing Spots
types.visual_character: The quintessential Turing pattern — perfectly arranged negative spots (dark holes) in a hexagonal lattice on a light field. Calm, geometric, almost crystalline. Strikingly similar to cheetah spots, leopard skin, or the eye pattern on a butterfly wing. The geometry feels inevitable, like close-packing of circles.
types.emergence_behavior: Emerges from uniform noise after ~2000–4000 iterations via symmetry-breaking instability. The hexagonal arrangement crystallizes gradually — spots nucleate, jostle into position, and then freeze. Truly static once settled.
types.visual_scale: Spot diameter ~15–25 pixels at 512². Center-to-center spacing ~25–35 pixels.
types.density: Regular. Spots occupy ~30% of field, background ~70%.

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: sharp peaks 0.2–0.45 at spot centers, near-0 background
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: ivory/cream background with dark spots — classic cheetah palette; or gold background with black spots for leopard
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Map V>0.15 to spot color, V<0.05 to background. Sharp threshold = graphic look; smooth = biological look.

types.name: Chaotic Mitosis
types.visual_character: A constantly changing field of spots that grow, elongate, pinch, and split like dividing cells — then do it all over again. Some spots merge; others escape as rings that travel across the field. Chaotic, alive, reminiscent of time-lapse biology. The closest reaction-diffusion pattern to actual cell division.
types.emergence_behavior: Begins with a few spots from the seed. Each spot grows spherically until it elongates along a longer axis and pinches into two daughter spots (mitosis). The daughters then repeat the cycle. Chaotic because the splitting direction and timing vary unpredictably. Never reaches steady state.
types.visual_scale: Spots 10–30 pixels diameter, vary widely. Field constantly restructuring.
types.density: Variable 20–50% V-occupied. Fluctuates as spots split and merge.

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: dark magenta spots on black, or green blobs on dark — laboratory microscopy aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Animate with du/dt channel to highlight splitting moments in white — dramatic for video.

types.name: Stable Chaotic Spots
types.visual_character: Similar to epsilon's mitotic spots but calmer and more symmetrical. The spots divide less frequently and maintain more regular shapes between events. Think of cells in a slowly growing colony versus a tumor — orderly enough to be beautiful, alive enough to keep moving.
types.emergence_behavior: Spot pattern emerges and undergoes mitosis, but with longer pause times between splits. Subtle pulsing oscillation of spot size is visible. Eventually reaches a near-steady state with only occasional reorganization events.
types.visual_scale: Spots 15–25 pixels diameter. More regular than ε.
ai_prompt_keywords: ordered spot pattern with subtle motion

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: peaks at spot centers, smooth gradients outward
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: olive or amber spots on cream — frog skin or turtle shell aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Use Gaussian blur on V before coloring to soften spot edges for a biological photograph look.

types.name: Spots and Worms
types.visual_character: A rich mixed pattern: spots and short worm-like stripes coexist in the same field, creating an irregular, naturalistic texture. Some regions are spot-dominated, others stripe-dominated, creating apparent 'territories'. Like the flank of a giraffe where spots and stripes blend at transitions.
types.emergence_behavior: Initially active with both spot and stripe formation. Oscillates periodically during development then reaches a stable mixed steady state. The boundary regions between spot and stripe zones are particularly complex.
types.visual_scale: Spots 15–20px, worm segments 10–15px wide, 20–40px long. Mix varies across field.
types.density: Moderate to high. 40–60% of field in V-rich state.
ai_prompt_keywords: organic mixed blob and worm texture

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: variable peaks in spots and stripes, 0.2–0.45
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: warm ochre and brown on cream — giraffe or dalmatian aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Color spots and stripes differently by using V gradient magnitude as a secondary channel.

types.name: Ring Growth Stripes
types.visual_character: Blue seed spots expand as expanding rings, then the rings solidify into concentric stripe networks. The final pattern looks like tree rings, topographic contours, or the growth rings visible in a cut tree trunk. Static and geometric.
types.emergence_behavior: Each initial seed point becomes a growing ring. As rings from different centers meet, they form complex interference patterns that eventually freeze into the concentric stripe network. Very characteristic transient ring phase before reaching steady state.
types.visual_scale: Ring spacing ~12–20 pixels. Large concentric structures (100–200px diameter) centered on seed points.
types.density: Medium-high stripe density once settled. 50–60% V-occupied.
ai_prompt_keywords: interference ring pattern frozen in time

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: warm amber concentric bands on dark brown — agate stone or tree ring aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Map V to a stepped (quantized) colormap for topographic contour effect.

types.name: Molecular Negatons
types.visual_character: Small, discrete, negative-space objects — dark spots on a light field — that interact at distance like molecules. They repel each other and maintain characteristic spacing without merging. Resembles a 2D gas of hard-sphere molecules, or the dot pattern of a grainy photograph.
types.emergence_behavior: Negatons (negative spots, low-V islands in high-V sea) form quickly and reach a stable, non-mitotic configuration. They drift very slowly and interact electrostatically (via diffusion fields). True steady-state class 2 behavior.
types.visual_scale: Negaton diameter ~8–15 pixels. Characteristic separation distance ~25–40 pixels.
types.density: Low V. Negatons are dark spots (low V) on bright background. ~15–25% negaton coverage.

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: high background ~0.25, dips to near-0 at negaton centers
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: bright white/cyan background with dark blue or black negatons — scientific imaging aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Invert V channel for positive spots. Threshold V<0.08 to isolate negaton positions as a point field.

types.name: Hedgerow Mazes
types.visual_character: Long, meandering stripes that bifurcate, dead-end, and form disconnected maze-like networks. The labyrinthine topology is reminiscent of hedge mazes, river delta channels from altitude, or the branching pattern of lightning. No closed loops — the topology is tree-like.
types.emergence_behavior: Stripes grow from seed points, bifurcate at angles, and stop when they approach other stripes. The maze topology is fixed once growth terminates — a class 2-a static pattern. Very slow convergence, may take 5000–10000 iterations.
types.visual_scale: Stripe width ~10–15 pixels, maze corridors ~15–25 pixels wide. Branching events every 50–100 pixels.

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: dark green stripes on light tan — hedge maze; or dark blue on white — river delta map
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Skeletonize the V threshold image to get pure 1-pixel maze walls for graph analysis.

types.name: Mitotic Hexagons
types.visual_character: Round soliton spots that divide and self-organize into a near-perfect hexagonal grid. The end state is a crystalline, honeycomb-like arrangement — more ordered than the chaos of epsilon, more biological than the cold lattice of delta. Like a carefully grown soap bubble raft.
types.emergence_behavior: Spots emerge, undergo mitotic division, then migrate into hexagonal equilibrium positions. The crystallization process involves long-range rearrangement as each spot senses its neighbors. Final static state is a near-perfect triangular lattice.
types.visual_scale: Spot diameter ~18–25 pixels. Lattice spacing ~30–40 pixels.

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: sharp peaks at lattice points 0.3–0.5, near-0 background
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: golden honeycomb yellow spots on dark brown — bee's wax aesthetic; or white spots on black for stark scientific look
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Voronoi diagram of spot centers overlaid on the pattern reveals the hexagonal lattice geometry perfectly.

types.name: Growing Worms
types.visual_character: Long, parallel worm-like stripes that grow from their ends and reorganize until they run parallel. The final state is a beautiful, regular striped pattern — like rows of noodles or a corduroy fabric. More regular and longer than gamma's unstable stripes.
types.emergence_behavior: Short worm stubs appear from seed and elongate from both ends. They steer toward parallelism, avoiding head-on collisions. The reorganization process is slow and satisfying to watch. Final static state is a grid of parallel stripes.
types.visual_scale: Stripe width ~10–15 pixels, parallel spacing ~20–30 pixels. Very long (can span entire domain).
types.density: High regularity. ~45–55% V-covered in parallel stripes.

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: dark stripes on light background — zebra or barcode aesthetic; or warm/cool alternation for woven fabric feel
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Apply orientation coloring (using V gradient direction) to turn uniform stripes into rainbow-oriented worm field.

types.name: Inert Solitons
types.visual_character: Isolated, perfectly stable spots that neither divide nor die — they just exist, very slowly drifting apart under exponential repulsion. The quietest, most isolated of all spot types. Like atoms frozen in a diffuse lattice, or isolated bubbles in thick viscous fluid that barely move.
types.emergence_behavior: Solitons form from the seed and immediately stabilize. No mitosis. No oscillation. They drift apart on logarithmic timescales — effectively static on human-observation timescales. True class 2 behavior.
types.visual_scale: Soliton diameter ~12–20 pixels. Widely separated, characteristic distance ~50–100 pixels depending on initial density.

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: pure black background with small glowing spots — starfield or lava lamp aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Render only V>0.1 as bright; map rest to pure black for a starfield or particle system look.

types.name: Spirals
types.visual_character: Large, majestic, sustained spiral waves similar to the Belousov-Zhabotinsky chemical reaction. Multiple spiral arms rotate around organizing centers. The field looks like a galaxy, a hurricane viewed from space, or a pinwheel galaxy of chemical activity. Continuously rotating.
types.emergence_behavior: Spirals emerge from initial wavelet chaos and grow to fill the domain. Multiple spiral cores form and compete — faster-rotating spirals consume slower ones in a process called 'spiral selection'. Sustained oscillation indefinitely.
types.visual_scale: Spiral arm spacing ~20–35 pixels. Large spiral extent can span 50–30% of the domain.
types.density: Variable across spiral arms. 0.1–0.4 V throughout.

color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: cyclic colormap (HSV or twilight) for spirals — colors complete a full rotation for each wave cycle
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Phase-coloring with atan2(gradient_v, gradient_u) reveals spiral topology. Time-animate the phase offset for hypnotic rotation effect.

types.name: U-Skate World
types.visual_character: The most computationally complex of all Pearson types — stable, self-propelled localized structures that move through the field like autonomous agents. Each 'U-skate' is a small shape that maintains itself and moves at constant velocity. The field is a complex ecology of these moving entities. Wolfram class 4 — the edge of chaos, computationally universal.
types.emergence_behavior: From initial seeds, complex localized moving structures emerge after extended transients (3000–8000 iterations). Once formed, they persist indefinitely, sometimes colliding and annihilating, sometimes spawning new ones. The pattern is chaotic but structured — like a billiard table of self-propelled particles.
types.visual_scale: U-skate units: ~15–25 pixels. Complex internal structure. Move at ~0.1–0.3 pixels per iteration.
types.density: Sparse to moderate. Complex dynamic density fluctuations.

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: complex localized structures 0–0.5 with moving boundaries
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: dark field with vivid moving structures — Matrix green on black, or high-contrast scientific colormap
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Track individual U-skate positions over time and color by trajectory for path visualization art.

types.name: Red Soap Bubbles
types.visual_character: Closed, roughly circular regions of the red (low-U) state, bordered by blue stripes. The interiors are chemically distinct from the exterior — true topological regions with 'surface tension' behavior. Looks like soap bubble foam, dried paint cells, or Voronoi cells.
types.emergence_behavior: Regions of low-U state nucleate and grow, but their boundaries (stripes) prevent them from merging until direct contact. The resulting closed-cell foam topology is static once formed. Very high feed rate stabilizes the structure quickly.
types.visual_scale: Bubble diameter 30–80 pixels depending on initial conditions. Borders ~10px wide.
types.density: Complex topology. Bubble interiors occupy 30–60% of field.

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: high inside borders, low inside bubbles
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: warm red-orange interiors with cool blue borders — soap film iridescence aesthetic
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Extract bubble borders only (V threshold) for a Voronoi/stained-glass coloring schema.

types.name: Blue Soap Bubbles
types.visual_character: Twin of rho but inverted — closed blue (high-U) regions bordered by narrow stripes. The blue bubbles have a cooler, cleaner aesthetic than the red bubbles of rho. Like cells in a microscope image, or the light cells in a stained-glass window.
types.emergence_behavior: Same topological bubble formation as rho but with inverted chemical character. Blue regions (high U) nucleate and expand. Borders are negative stripes (low V). Static class 2-a.
types.visual_scale: Bubble diameter 30–80 pixels. Narrower borders than rho (~8px).

color_mapping_recommendations.V_field: minimal inside cells, high at borders
color_mapping_recommendations.suggested_palette: pale ice-blue cells with dark indigo borders — stained glass aesthetic; or white cells on midnight blue
color_mapping_recommendations.contrast_tip: Invert from rho: where rho is warm, sigma is cool. Perfect pair for diptych or complementary texture sets.
